characteristics.oxidation: Minimal, with a smothering stage and subtle smoking
characteristics.roast: Light pine-wood smoking during the final drying phase

description.short: Rare yellow tea with a delicate smoky whisper from traditional pine wood drying
description.overview: One of the very few yellow teas incorporating a gentle smoking element — an unusual marriage for a category universally renowned for delicate sweetness rather than smokiness.
description.leaf: Twisted downy needle-like leaves of a deep amber-yellow hue
description.taste: Sweet, with gentle delicate smokiness, free of harshness
description.aftertaste: Soft, with a subtle lingering smoky nuance
description.processing: Plucking → pan-firing fixation → moist smothering (men huang) → rolling → drying over smoldering pine firewood (imparting subtle smoke)

history.origin: Produced in the Mount Weishan area of Hunan province, historically linked with the local Buddhist Miyin Temple on Mount Weishan.
history.development: Final open-fire pine smoking represents a preserved archaic technique inherited from traditional processing before modern drying machinery.
history.modern: One of the least known regional yellow teas outside China, produced in strictly limited quantities.
interestingFacts: Its smoky note draws curious comparisons to smoked black teas like traditional Zheng Shan Xiao Zhong (Lapsang Souchong), even though the categories and processing pathways are completely distinct.
Yellow tea remains the rarest of the six classical Chinese tea types, and unique regional variations like Weishan Maojian are rarely encountered beyond Hunan.
